In the VDOE guidance, cell phone-free education is the age-appropriate elimination or restriction of cell phones and other personal electronic communication devices in public schools.

Personal electronic communication device definition is any personal device that connects to a smartphone, internet, cellular Wi-Fi network, or similar devices, including smartwatches, headphones, laptops, and tablets. And stored means devices are not carried on the student's person.

For example, it's in a backpack, locker, locked pouch, or designated classroom area. According to the VDOE guidance, each public school system must establish clear procedures for offsite events or activities, including all school sponsored events or field trips and transportation.

During instructional time, students must use school-based communication tools in the office, classroom, or other centralized location to communicate non-emergency needs with parents. Parents should use school-based communication tools and channels to communicate emergencies during instructional time.

And if a student travels to a different campus during the school day, they must adhere to the building's policy and procedures for cell phones and personal electronic communication devices. According to the VDOE guidance, public schools must consider students with a disability, L students with a documented language barrier, students' IEPs and 504 plans when creating policies regarding cell phone and personal electronic communication device access, usage and storage protocols, and should provide school-based devices for assistive technology where appropriate.

School divisions must publicly share how school-based personnel are trained to manage crisis and emergency situations, reunification plans and family notification processes during crisis situations. Public schools should notify parents at the start of the school year about any updates to the annual crisis emergency plan, and clearly outline the communications plan for parent notification, should a school-based emergency or crisis occur, including any relevant or timely follow-up information regarding a school-based emergency event.

The VDOE guidance recommends that school divisions be clear in their emergency communication protocols, whether or not students can access their stored cell phone and/or personal electronic communication device during a school-based emergency, and communicate this policy clearly to parents and students, training and communication plans should be updated.
